thread:
Ravi: Hey, brand-new account, ran the CLI quickstart for private deployment. first POST to /v1/chat fails with `curl: (60) SSL: certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate`. dashboard shows workspace active and a tiny billing notice in the corner saying 'add payment method', so i assumed billing blocked calls. anyone seen this interplay? :thinking:

Sam: that curl error is pure TLS verification. billing toasts shouldn't affect the TLS stack. can you paste `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.local:443 -showcerts` output (redact IPs)? also which OS/openssl version?

Ravi: paste (redacted): ```CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private.redwood.local
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=private.redwood.local
   i:/CN=Internal-Dev-CA
---
```

Aisha: looks like the server presents a cert signed by an internal CA that your machine doesn't trust. quickstart for private customers requires adding the internal CA to the system trust store or using the `--cacert` flag for curl. for mac/linux quickstart we usually instruct to `sudo cp internal-ca.pem /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/ && sudo update-ca-certificates` (linux) or add to keychain on mac.

Ravi: thanks. i did `curl --cacert internal-ca.pem -v https://private.redwood.local/v1/chat` and the call worked and returned 200. but curious: why did the UI show the payment toast at the same time? it's confusing for onboarding.

billing-ops: we show a non-modal billing hint when workspace billing is in a default/unknown state. that can overlap with other errors. agree it's confusing if it looks like the cause.

devex-bot: Created DX ticket DX-1377: "Private quickstart: add CA verification step and suppress billing toast when TLS handshake fails on first-call". Suggested changes: quickstart CLI checks (openssl s_client) and clear message: 'TLS verify failed: your machine does not trust the private deploy CA'. Link: https://internal.docs/redwood/devex/private-quickstart-ca

Sam: for immediate relief we can update the quickstart script to detect a 60-like curl exit and show a help line: "If you see a certificate verify error, try --cacert ... or add the CA to your trust store". also add a note in console logs that billing toast is advisory and not necessarily the failure reason.

Aisha: security note: adding a CA to system trust is sensitive; include a clear revert step in the docs and recommend using a local `--cacert` for testers when possible.

Ravi: fixed it with `--cacert`. I'll follow up with a short PR to the quickstart repo adding a one-liner and the openssl command. thanks all! :raised_hands:
